agua-zarca-berta-caceres.conditions_add: FMO, the Dutch development bank that lent US$15 million to the dam company DESA with Finnfund, says on its own Agua Zarca page that it "signed a credit agreement with DESA in 2014, including ESG requirements", and that regular site visits before and throughout construction checked that the plant was being built in line with those environmental, social and governance requirements. FMO does not publish the requirements themselves: its project FAQ gives the loan amount and describes annual monitoring trips and quarterly visits by independent advisers, but lists no conditions precedent, covenants or action plan.

why.safeguard: signed a credit agreement with DESA in 2014, including ESG requirements

agua-zarca-berta-caceres.searched: Switched lender: the IFC/CAMIF link was already shown to be undocumented, so this round read FMO's own project page and project FAQ (fmo.nl serves normally). The page states that the 2014 credit agreement with DESA included ESG requirements; the FAQ names only the US$15 million loan and FMO's monitoring, with no list of covenants. CABEI, the largest lender, publishes no document for the loan.

kalangala-oil-palm.conditions_add: The lender of record is IFAD, not the World Bank, and IFAD's own President's Report for the second phase of the Vegetable Oil Development Project (SDR 33.5 million, about US$52 million, put to the Executive Board in April 2010) lists the conditions on the money. As conditions precedent to withdrawal, IFAD had to accept the appointed project manager and financial controller, the agriculture ministry had to set up a contracts committee with delegated authority over procurement, and draft guidelines for oilseeds and oil palm development and a project operations and financial management manual had to be submitted to IFAD. A covenant states that "No new oil palm development shall be undertaken on the outlying islands or Buvuma Island" until environmental impact assessments were carried out and a compliance certificate issued, and funds for smallholder planting on the outlying islands and for the oilseed guarantee fund were subject to prior approval by the Fund (IFAD, EB 2010/99/R.19).

why.admin: a project operations and financial management manual had to be submitted to IFAD
why.safeguard: No new oil palm development shall be undertaken on the outlying islands or Buvuma Island
why.fincov: were subject to prior approval by the Fund

sources_add.title: Report of the President to the Executive Board on a proposed loan to the Republic of Uganda for the Vegetable Oil Development Project - Phase 2 (EB 2010/99/R.19)

kalangala-oil-palm.searched: Dropped the World Bank route, which the last round showed has no document for this project, and went to the actual lender. IFAD's Executive Board document store (webapps.ifad.org, which redirects to members.ifad.org) serves: EB 2010/99/R.19 fetched in full and carries the conditions precedent to withdrawal, the disbursement conditions in Schedule 2 and the covenants in Schedule 3. Note the report does not set a condition about land acquisition or compensation on Bugala Island itself.

upper-atbara-setit-arab-funds.conditions_add: The Arab Fund's own project record for loan 557, KD 50 million signed on 28 March 2011 with Sudan's Dams Implementation Unit, gives the terms: 2.5 per cent interest, a seven-year grace period, 25-year maturity and repayment in 37 semi-annual instalments. The loan covers about 11 per cent of the project's KD 443.7 million cost, and the record states that "The Government of Sudan will cover the remaining cost of the project and any additional cost that may arise". The page lists no other requirement: it mentions that the project includes compensation for properties and the resettlement of 138,000 inhabitants, but does not say the Arab Fund required or financed that work.

why.fincov: The Government of Sudan will cover the remaining cost of the project and any additional cost that may arise

sources_add.title: Complex Dams of Upper Atbara and Setit (Republic of Sudan)
sources_add.publisher: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development

upper-atbara-setit-arab-funds.searched: arabfund.org project pages serve and were read for the first time this round: the record for loan 557 gives the amount, date, financial terms and the counterpart-funding obligation, and no other condition. The Arab Fund publishes no appraisal report or loan agreement, and the OPEC Fund, Kuwait Fund, Saudi Fund, Islamic Development Bank and Abu Dhabi Fund records give amounts and dates only.

libya-coast-guard-eu-italy-detention.conditions_add: The European Commission's action document for the EU Trust Fund programme "Support to Integrated Border and Migration Management in Libya" (EUR 42,223,927.28 to Italy's Ministry of the Interior under indirect management, reference Ares(2019)7307599) makes parts of the money conditional. For the southern border activity it states that "The financing and completion of the activity will be conditional to the results of such assessment", and it states that "The financing of border control facilities will be also conditional to a progressive access of humanitarian actors". It also records that "The Libyan authorities have to commit not to move the personnel, once they are trained, to a different office/body", requires the Italian ministry to produce a progress report every four months including a conflict sensitivity analysis, and says regular assessments "will constitute a basis for a possible decision of suspension of activities".

why.fincov: The financing of border control facilities will be also conditional to a progressive access of humanitarian actors
why.admin: requires the Italian ministry to produce a progress report every four months including a conflict sensitivity analysis

sources_add.title: Action Document for the EU Trust Fund for Africa: Support to Integrated Border and Migration Management in Libya (Annex 3.6, DG NEAR)
sources_add.publisher: European Commission, released via Privacy International

libya-coast-guard-eu-italy-detention.searched: New route: the EU Trust Fund action documents released by Privacy International fetch in full (data.privacyinternational.org, after a redirect from privacyinternational.org). The action document for the Libya border and migration management programme carries explicit conditionality on the financing, a commitment required of the Libyan authorities, reporting obligations and a suspension basis. trust-fund-for-africa.europa.eu carries only programme summaries.

barkagaon-ntpc-firing-2016.searched: The requirement found is a term on the intermediary bank's own IFC facility, not on this project. The Summary of Proposed Investment for IFC project 25492 (ICICI Bank UT2, a US$150 million subordinated Upper Tier II loan signed 22 December 2006) was re-read on disclosures.ifc.org, which serves normally; its only requirement is that the bank formalise a Social and Environmental Management System and apply IFC's exclusion list and Performance Standard 2 to its own portfolio. Nothing in that document, and nothing in Inclusive Development International's report, shows that the IFC-funded facility was the money that reached NTPC and its Pakri-Barwadih captive mine - the bank's lending here was general corporate finance, not an earmarked sub-loan - so the step from IFC's money to this project is undocumented and the case is left blank. No separate IFC project page exists for this operation.

el-dorado-fontibon-noise.searched: Took a third route and it carries no term. interagua-guayaquil.searched: A date mismatch rules out the one document that does carry terms. idbinvest.org serves and its page for the Interagua corporate loan gives US$70 million approved 15 December 2016 and signed 5 December 2018, with commitments to achieve service targets on water pressure, continuity, supply and water quality - but that loan comes after the 2001-2011 harm, so its terms cannot be attached to this case. The earlier IDB Guayaquil loans are documented only on iadb.org, which refuses.

poland-nowa-huta-1988.searched: Settled as a finding rather than a failure, and re-stated here so it is not searched again: the World Bank documents API serves and returns no adjustment-lending document for Poland around 1988-1990. Poland joined the Bank and the Fund in June 1986 and Bank adjustment lending began only after the 1989 change of government, so there is no 1988 loan or programme whose conditions could bear on the Nowa Huta strike. The price reform of 1987-88 was the Polish government's own, adopted in the hope of later debt relief, which is not a lender condition.

BankTrack serves and gives the tranche structure - Standard Bank, Stanbic Bank Uganda and KCB Bank Uganda at US$200 million each, Afreximbank and the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector at US$200 million each, and a US$100 million Islamic facility from the Islamic Development Bank - sourced to IJGlobal, but no covenant, condition precedent or security term. messok-dja-baka-ecoguards.searched: Read the right document and it says the requirements were policy, not terms of the money. UNDP's SECU final investigation report (SECU0009, on info.undp.org, which serves) attributes the screening, Indigenous Peoples Plan and free, prior and informed consent requirements to UNDP's own Social and Environmental Standards, and states at paragraph 23 that "UNDP is not required to ensure compliance with the SES of activities that are not funded through UNDP accounts". It records that the project document makes no reference to those standards and that no Indigenous Peoples Plan was prepared, and it describes the UNDP-WWF letters of agreement as carrying delivery indicators such as patrol and arrest counts, not safeguard conditions. The Global Environment Facility grant's own terms are not published and the report names none.

guatemala-std-inoculation-1946.searched: Not a loan and no agreement exists to read. The money was a 1946-48 US Public Health Service research grant routed through the Pan American Sanitary Bureau to Guatemalan ministries; the US government's own accounts of the episode describe the funding route but publish no grant instrument, and no condition attached to the grant is recorded anywhere. Nothing new was tried on the document routes named in the brief because none of them covers 1940s US bilateral research grants.

somsanga-drug-detention-laos.searched: The funding was a series of small bilateral and UN agency grants - US$145,786 for a clinic, a US$95,200 renovation, US$22,500, US$10,000 and US$9,300 contributions - and no grant agreement or funding instrument for any of them is published, so there is no document in which a condition could appear. The US State Department, UNODC, Japanese, Singaporean, German and Australian records that describe the payments give purposes and amounts only.

choam-chao-unicef-youth-centre.searched: UNICEF gave unspecified "limited funding" through Cambodia's Ministry of Social Affairs and publishes no grant agreement or amount for the Choam Chao centre, so there is no instrument whose terms could be reported. UNICEF's own account states only that it supported the centre from 2006 and stopped funding after confirming abuse reports, which is a withdrawal rather than a condition.

desert-dumps-eu-north-africa.searched: A conditions document was found but it belongs to a different EU action. The EU action document for the Multi-Country Migration Programme for the Southern Neighbourhood (CRIS NDICI-GEO-NEAR/2021/043-487, EUR 45 million, of which EUR 25 million for Tunisia), released by Statewatch and read in full this round, does set terms: "The action can only be implemented with persons who are not on the sanctions list", only EU-based partners may deliver the equipment and training to prevent its misuse, and it states that it is "not envisaged to conclude a financing agreement with the partner countries". But that money funds a maritime training academy, a rescue coordination centre and coastal surveillance in Tunisia, not the EU Trust Fund money for migration management that this case describes, and it covers Libya and Tunisia only, not Morocco or Mauritania. Attaching it here would be a term from a different grant, so the case is left blank; the next round can use it if the case's scope is widened.

unicef-tube-wells-bangladesh-arsenic.searched: UNICEF worked with Bangladesh's Department of Public Health Engineering to install tube-wells from the 1970s under a grant programme for which no agreement, amount or funding instrument is published, and the account of its role comes from a WHO Bulletin article rather than a funding document. There is no document in which a condition on the money could be recorded, and the private suppliers who installed most of the later wells had no UNICEF funding at all.

virunga-eu-rangers-residents.searched: Read the EU's own announcement of the grant and it carries no term. The European Commission's capacity4dev page for the EUR 53 million grant signed on 28 November 2016 between the EU, the DRC government and the Virunga Foundation (of which EUR 15.4 million comes from the 11th European Development Fund national indicative programme) states the purpose and the five-year term and nothing about conditions, obligations on the foundation or the government, spending restrictions, reporting or oversight. The contribution agreement itself is not published, and no EU action document for the grant could be found.
